channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em artigo no Washington Post, Lula diz que ninguém 'vai nos derrotar com base em mentiras'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) published an article in The Washington Post criticizing U.S. tariffs on Brazilian imports as being based on lies, stating Brazil is considering retaliatory measures, while inviting the Trump administration to continue dialogue.

item.title: Ronaldo Caiado tenta pela 2ª vez ser presidente do Brasil, após 37 anos
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, former senator and governor of Goiás, has been chosen as the PSD's presidential candidate for 2026 after the withdrawal of Ratinho Junior and a victory over Eduardo Leite in the party's internal dispute. At 76, he is making his second attempt to reach the presidency, having received less than 1% of the vote in the 1989 election. His career includes leadership in the UDR, multiple terms as federal deputy, senator, and two terms as governor of Goiás, consistently opposing the PT.

item.title: PSD lança candidatura de Ronaldo Caiado à Presidência da República
item.description: The Social Democratic Party (PSD) officially nominated Ronaldo Caiado as its presidential candidate at a national convention in São Paulo, with Gilberto Kassab as his running mate. Caiado emphasized his record as governor of Goiás, where he left office with 88% approval, and pledged a 'new model of government' focused on results and courage to overcome political polarization. The ticket is composed solely of PSD members, with no coalitions finalized so far.

item.title: Com pré-candidatura a presidente em xeque, Aldo Rebelo vai à convenção de Caiado
item.description: Aldo Rebelo, pre-candidate of the Christian Democracy party (DC) for president, attended the PSD national convention that formalized Ronaldo Caiado’s presidential bid. He praised Caiado’s presence as elevating the quality of the presidential debate and reiterated his own presidential ambitions despite an internal party dispute that replaced his name with former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa, a move he has challenged in court. Aldo stated that, if he secures his candidacy, his priority would be to 'unblock' Brazil, criticizing the STF, Public Ministry, Ibama, Funai, and ICMBio for allegedly paralyzing the country, and emphasized the need to discuss public security and education.

item.title: 'Ninguém vai nos derrotar com base em mentiras', diz Lula em artigo no jornal Washington Post
item.description: President Lula published an article in The Washington Post criticizing U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods as a strategic mistake and denying allegations of electoral interference, stating that 'no one will defeat us based on lies'. He emphasized his direct negotiations with Trump and warned that the tariffs harm both the U.S. economy and bilateral relations. Brazil denied visas to two U.S. State Department officials who, according to reports, intended to question the integrity of Brazil's electoral system.

item.title: Lula diz a jornal que tem mecanismos de reciprocidade para lidar com tarifas de Trump
item.description: President Lula stated that U.S. tariffs on Brazil are a strategic error and said Brazil has mechanisms to ensure reciprocity. He published an article in The Washington Post defending Brazil's position against U.S. trade measures.

item.title: Explorada por Flávio, inflação dos alimentos foi munição de Lula contra Bolsonaro em 2022
item.description: The content shows that food inflation and the cost of living were used as political themes both by Lula in 2022 against Bolsonaro and by Flávio Bolsonaro now against the Lula government, highlighting a mutual exchange of accusations over responsibility for rising prices. In April 2022, Lula used the symbol of an empty basic food basket to criticize Bolsonaro’s government, while Flávio Bolsonaro now does the same with videos in supermarkets and butcher shops, claiming that picanha — a symbol of the PT’s promise — has become too expensive. The narrative reveals a repeated strategy of exploiting public sensitivity to food costs to attack the opposing government.

item.title: "Comigo, bandido não se cria", diz Caiado antes de convenção do PSD em SP
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado officially launched his presidential bid under the PSD at a national convention in São Paulo, with Gilberto Kassab as his running mate. He positioned himself as a third-way alternative to Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, emphasizing his record on public safety and anti-corruption in Goiás, declaring: 'With me, criminals are not made. The PT is not made.' Caiado has intensified attacks on his rivals, accusing Lula of avoiding debates and Flávio Bolsonaro of lacking credibility due to scandals like the Banco Master case.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: como está o duelo Lula x Flávio após números da semana passada
item.description: Recent electoral polls (Real Time Big Data and Datafolha) maintain Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro in both the first and second rounds, with no significant changes to the polarized landscape. Although Flávio showed a slight numerical recovery in the second round in Real Time Big Data (from 40% to 42%), the shift fell within the margin of error, repeating the technical tie pattern observed since March. The consolidated data from six national institutes confirms Lula’s consistent lead, with advantages ranging from 3 to 6 percentage points in the second round, while no other pre-candidate manages to break the bipolarity.

item.title: Lula critica tarifas de Trump ao Brasil: 'Ninguém nos vencerá com mentiras'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized, in a Washington Post opinion piece, the additional tariffs imposed by the United States on Brazilian goods, calling the measure unjust and based on misinformation. He stated that Brazil will not be defeated by lies and advocated for a balanced trade relationship with the U.S.

item.title: Lula usa o Palácio da Alvorada para reuniões de pré-campanha
item.description: President Lula has been using the Palácio da Alvorada for pre-campaign meetings, coordinated by PT national president Edinho Silva, with 15 to 20 attendees typically on Tuesdays. PT allies have expressed reservations about using government infrastructure for electoral purposes, arguing that a dedicated campaign committee would be more appropriate, though they acknowledge such practices were normalized in past elections, including Bolsonaro’s reelection bid. In a recent meeting, Lula had to mediate an internal PT conflict over the campaign’s legal team, personally asserting that Marco Aurélio de Carvalho — lawyer for Lulinha in INSS investigations and a longtime friend — must be included due to his strategic importance in shielding the Planalto from legal fallout.

item.title: Lula manda recado a Trump: "Ninguém nos derrotará com mentiras"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva published an article in The Washington Post criticizing U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, accusing the Trump administration of political motivation by referencing jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro. Lula argued the 37.5% tariffs are unjust, a strategic mistake that will harm the U.S. economy and bilateral trade, and warned against ideological or electoral instrumentalization of the relationship, concluding with: 'Nobody will defeat us with lies'.

item.title: TSE orienta tribunais a buscar apoio contra desinformação
item.description: The TSE directed regional electoral courts to establish technical cooperation agreements with institutions specializing in AI, digital forensics, and data analysis to counter disinformation in the 2026 elections. The initiative aims to enhance judicial evidence production through technological support while preserving judicial exclusivity in decision-making and upholding data protection and procedural secrecy.

item.title: EUA chamam suspeita de interferência no Brasil de “mentira”
item.description: The U.S. State Department dismissed allegations of electoral interference in Brazil as a 'baseless lie,' denying that a July visit by two officials aimed to undermine October's elections. Brazil's Itamaraty denied visas to the officials, citing concerns over undisclosed meetings with Flávio Bolsonaro and efforts to question the electronic voting system, while the U.S. maintained the trip was routine and focused on electoral integrity, religious freedom, and free speech. The incident follows the prior revocation of Darren Beattie's visa, a Trump ally, for an unreported meeting with former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Caiado se contrapõe a Flávio e defende urnas eletrônicas e não interferência dos EUA
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD presidential candidate, defended the integrity of Brazil's electronic voting machines and rejected any foreign interference, including from the U.S., in the 2026 election. He contrasted his position with that of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who had questioned the electoral system but later said he only sought international observers. Caiado noted the TSE will convene ambassadors on August 17 to uphold confidence in the system, while the OAS, EU, Parlasul, Carter Center, and ROJAE-CPLP are already confirmed to monitor the October 4 election.

item.title: Proposta fiscal de Flávio combina lei de Lula e MP vencida de Guedes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 economic proposal combines Lula's Complementary Law 208, allowing the sale of active debt tax credits, with the revival of Guedes' MP 1.137, which zeroed income tax for foreigners on private credit securities. Daniella Marques estimates raising R$150–250 billion from selling these credits, but the law mandates at least 50% go to pensions and the rest to investment, blocking direct debt amortization. To achieve the stated goal of reducing public debt, Flávio would need to change the law.

item.title: Meias verdades substituem mentiras e sofisticam a desinformação eleitoral, mostra estudo inédito
item.description: An unprecedented study reveals that half-truths — statements that are partially true but manipulated to mislead — are replacing outright lies as the primary tool of electoral disinformation in Brazil, making it increasingly difficult for voters to inform themselves accurately. The strategy, which has rapidly sophisticated in recent years, operates even without heavy reliance on artificial intelligence, emerging as a growing threat to democratic integrity just one week before the official start of the 2026 campaign.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio celebra trégua com Michelle, mas encrenca familiar é o recado que fica
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro apologized to Michelle Bolsonaro, who immediately accepted, bringing relief to his campaign. The truce was celebrated as a strategic victory, though the full article is noted as subscriber-only. While the familial reconciliation was highlighted, the underlying political context remains a silent but significant undertone.

item.title: O voto, dever ou direito? (por Gaudêncio Torquato)
item.description: Voting in Brazil is a civic duty under the Constitution, except for 16-18 year olds, those over 70, and illiterates, with penalties for unjustified abstention. The author contends that voluntary voting would not weaken democracy, noting that even with compulsory voting there is significant abstention, null, and blank votes, and that democracies like the U.S. and European nations function well without compulsory voting, where conscious participation leads to more qualified ballots.

item.title: 'Ninguém nos derrotará com mentiras', diz Lula a Trump em artigo no Washington Post sobre tarifaço
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva published an op-ed in The Washington Post criticizing new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods as politically motivated and harmful to global supply chains. He affirmed Brazil’s sovereignty, stating that the country’s future must be decided by Brazilians alone, without foreign interference, and highlighted progress in digital payment systems like Pix and aggressive environmental crime enforcement.

item.title: TSE fará nova reunião com embaixadores para defender urnas atacadas por Flávio
item.description: The TSE plans to meet with ambassadors on August 17 to defend the integrity of Brazil's electronic voting machines after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro used a diplomatic meeting to spread unfounded suspicions about the electoral system. Brazil has denied visas to two U.S. diplomats linked to the DRL who were allegedly planning to challenge the voting machines, and the TSE confirmed the U.S. Embassy will be invited to the new meeting, despite the U.S. lacking an ambassador in Brazil since January 2025.

item.title: Ausências na convenção de Caiado revelam pragmatismo eleitoral
item.description: The PSD convention ratifying Ronaldo Caiado as presidential candidate will be marked by notable absences of allies such as Raquel Lyra, Eduardo Paes, Mateus Simões and Tarcísio de Freitas, reflecting electoral pragmatism where parties prioritize federal deputy elections over presidential support. This shift is driven by public campaign financing and mandatory parliamentary amendments, making the race for the 513 Chamber seats more strategically important than the presidential contest.

item.title: Lindbergh critica convenção de Flávio: "Completamente fracassada"
item.description: Federal Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) harshly criticized the PL's national convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy, calling the event 'shameful' and 'completely failed'. He pointed out that Flávio appeared isolated, without party alliances, no vice-presidential running mate, and with the sole goal of freeing Jair Bolsonaro from prison. The convention featured allies such as Valdemar Costa Neto, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Ricardo Nunes, along with a speech by Javier Milei and an AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro endorsing Flávio as his successor.

item.title: A relação 'Tom & Jerry' entre Michelle e Flávio, segundo um político próximo aos Bolsonaro
item.description: A politician close to the Bolsonaro family describes the relationship between Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro as resembling the Tom and Jerry dynamic, stating that Flávio avoided speaking with Michelle after being launched as a candidate by his father, ignoring her completely despite repeated urging from Valdemar Costa Neto to seek her support.

item.title: EUA negam que visita de emissários ao Brasil buscava interferir na eleição
item.description: The U.S. State Department denied that a visit by two officials to Brazil aimed to interfere in the 2026 elections, stating the trip was purely diplomatic in nature. The statement came after Brazil’s Itamaraty denied entry visas to the U.S. officials, sparking speculation about bilateral tensions. The Brazilian government has not issued an official comment on the incident so far.

item.title: Caiado diz ser “inadmissível” dúvida sobre lisura das eleições brasileiras
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pré-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated it is ‘inadmissible’ to cast doubt on the integrity of Brazilian elections, amid speculation about a possible U.S. observer mission for the 2026 vote. He emphasized that electoral integrity is fundamental to democracy.

item.title: Com Jair Bolsonaro preso, parentes enfrentam obstáculos ao tentar ocupar espaço político
item.description: In 2026, multiple relatives of Jair Bolsonaro are seeking political office to capitalize on bolsonarismo following his ineligibility and imprisonment for attempting a coup. Flávio Bolsonaro is running for president, while Carlos, Eduardo, Jair Renan, Michelle Bolsonaro, Renato Bolsonaro, and Rogéria are contesting congressional seats. Despite early electoral strength, Michelle faces high rejection (23.9%) and internal conflict with Flávio, creating uncertainty about her Senate bid in the Federal District.

item.title: Em Minas, Lula terá de superar falta de apoio do centro e legado ruim do PT
item.description: In Minas Gerais, in Minas Gerais to build a competitive ticket after the refusal of Rodrigo Pacheco and the impossibility of an alliance with Alexandre Kalil and Gabriel Azevedo. The selection of Patrus Ananias as the gubernatorial candidate, while symbolic due to his historical role in Lula’s administrations, eliminates chances of centrist or right-wing alliances. The Lula ticket will rely only on traditional allies (PSB, PSOL, Rede), limiting its appeal to conservative and moderate voters in a state crucial for the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Caiado lança candidatura com desafio de atacar bolsonarismo e buscar ‘voto útil’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado launched his presidential candidacy aiming to capture the so-called 'useful vote' by attacking Flávio Bolsonaro's lack of managerial experience and criticizing the Bolsonaro family's tariff policies, while attempting to win over right-wing voters with an amnesty discourse. Despite this, his voting intentions remain low (between 3% and 7% in polls), reflecting the difficulty of overcoming Bolsonaro's dominance on the right and surpassing Lula's leadership. Caiado seeks to position himself as a viable alternative in a potential runoff, should Flávio Bolsonaro continue to decline.

item.title: Michelle se mostra superior a Flávio até no digital
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro demonstrated digital superiority over Flávio Bolsonaro by reaching 8.4 million views in an apology video, compared to just 1.3 million for the senator, highlighting her organic appeal versus his artificial candidacy. The episode, involving public apologies and family tensions within the Bolsonaro clan, provoked indignation in Carlos Bolsonaro and underscored Flávio’s isolation within his own party.

item.title: Letícia Barros na Crusoé: Mulheres votam mal?
item.description: Letícia Barros, columnist at Crusoé, analyzes a growing movement in Brazilian politics advocating for the end of women's voting rights, based on statements by political influencers and proposals like the 'family vote' from the MBL. This trend prompted the Women's Caucus to file a complaint with the Attorney General's Office (PGR), arguing the rhetoric is discriminatory and dangerous to democracy.

item.title: Deputada do PT aciona PGR por vídeo de IA de Bolsonaro
item.description: Federal Deputy Dandara (PT-MG) has requested the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to open an investigation into an AI-generated video featuring Jair Bolsonaro, shown at the PL party convention that formally launched Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential candidacy. The lawmaker argues the video may constitute ideological falsity and the improper use of AI for electoral purposes, violating Brazilian election law. The incident raises concerns about the growing use of deepfakes in political campaigns.

item.title: Quem são os funcionários americanos que tiveram visto negado pelo Itamaraty
item.description: Brazil's Itamaraty denied visas to U.S. State Department officials Riley Bernes and Samuel Samson, claiming their visit could raise doubts about the reliability of Brazil's electoral system. The U.S. State Department rejected the accusation as baseless, stating the trip was a routine mission to discuss electoral integrity, religious freedom, and freedom of expression. The decision followed allegations by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro about electronic voting machines, which have been debunked by the TSE.

item.title: BB simplifica abertura de contas eleitorais para 2026
item.description: Banco do Brasil has simplified the opening of electoral accounts for the 2026 elections, allowing candidates to open up to five fully digital accounts via its app using only an ID and facial biometric validation. The innovation integrates the bank’s system with the Electoral Justice for automatic validation of the RAC, reducing bureaucracy and increasing speed. The account is mandatory for campaign financing and aims to ensure transparency, security, and legal compliance.

item.title: Caiado repudia possibilidade de EUA questionar eleições no Brasil
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado rejected the U.S. attempt to send observers to question the integrity of Brazil's elections, stating he trusts the electronic voting system and finds it unacceptable for any country, including the U.S., to cast doubt on the electoral process. He affirmed support for international observers but condemned efforts to delegitimize the vote.

item.title: Milei dança com Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei danced with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) on stage at the PL national convention in São Paulo, where Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy was officially launched. The duo danced to 'Panic Show' by Argentine band La Renga, a song frequently used in Milei’s events.

item.title: Lula foca em aumentar aprovação do governo antes do início da campanha
item.description: President Lula is focused on boosting government approval in polls before the official start of the 2026 election campaign on August 16, aiming to reduce the need to defend his administration and instead highlight proposals and his legacy. Lula’s team believes the gradual improvement in approval ratings—shown in internal PT polls and the Quaest survey (48% approve vs. 47% disapprove)—stems from intensified public activities like trips, announcements, and deliveries, which they argue have greater impact than institutional government advertising.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential candidate, says he can be calmer and more moderate but insists on carrying the 'Bolsonaro blood' as his legacy. In an emotional message to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, he declares unconditional love and a commitment to honor his father's teachings and national representation until the end.

item.title: “Mentira sem fundamento”: EUA negam tentativa de interferir nas eleições brasileiras
item.description: The U.S. State Department denied that a planned diplomatic mission to Brazil aimed to interfere in the country’s elections, stating the visit was intended solely for routine bilateral discussions. The statement came after Brazil’s Itamaraty denied entry visas to two U.S. officials, sparking speculation about foreign influence in the electoral process.

item.title: Missão e Novo lideram doações com vaquinhas antes do início da campanha; veja ranking
item.description: Three weeks before the official start of the 2026 election campaigns, Renan Santos (Missão) leads online fundraising via 'vaquinhas' with R$1.1 million, followed by Jones Manoel (PSOL) with R$490,000 and Marcel van Hattem (Novo) with R$417,000, according to data from the TSE-homologated platform 'Quero Apoiar'. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: E a China, hein?
item.description: A survey of 1,650 readers shows that 93.2% support Brazil increasing its relations with China, while only 6.8% oppose it. The content also references articles and cartoons from Noblat’s Blog, including topics like Bolsonarism and foreign policy, but does not mention any specific candidates for the 2026 elections.

item.title: PT avalia acionar TSE contra vídeo com de IA de Bolsonaro em convenção
item.description: The PT is considering filing a complaint with the TSE over an AI-generated video shown at the PL convention that formalized Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy, featuring a deepfake of Jair Bolsonaro. The party argues the video may violate electoral regulations, as the TSE has specific rules governing AI use in campaigns. The clip, aired during a key moment of the event, depicts the former president endorsing Flávio as his successor using synthetic voice and image technology.

item.title: Lula aposta em alianças e PT será cabeça de chapa em 12 estados e DF
item.description: The PT will field its own gubernatorial candidates in 12 states and the Federal District in the 2026 elections, while supporting allied parties such as PSD, MDB, PP, União Brasil, PDT, and PSB elsewhere. Lula's strategy aims to secure strong electoral slates for his presidential reelection, prioritizing competitive alliances over fielding PT candidates in every state. This shift breaks from the PT's 1990s tradition of running many candidates, adopting a more pragmatic approach since 2002.

item.title: Relembre as vezes em que os EUA influenciaram a política no Brasil
item.description: The United States has a long history of involvement in Brazilian politics, dating back to World War II when it supported Getúlio Vargas’ government in exchange for military and economic cooperation, including the construction of CSN and the deployment of the FEB. During the Cold War, U.S. influence peaked with covert support for groups and logistical preparation for the 1964 coup against João Goulart, driven by fears of socialist leanings. In recent decades, the relationship has alternated between cooperation in investigations and diplomatic pressure, culminating in 2022 with a public U.S. defense of democratic institutions—only to see renewed tension under Trump’s second term over tariffs, Bolsonaro support, and the designation of PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reafirma obediência ao pai na convenção do “Sem, sem”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro was officially launched as the Liberal Party's presidential candidate at a convention in São Paulo, where he pledged lifelong obedience to his father Jair Bolsonaro, attacked Lula, the federal government, the PT, and Minister Alexandre de Moraes, and used an illegal AI-generated deepfake of his father. The event featured symbolic endorsements from Javier Milei and Benjamin Netanyahu, while the U.S. denied visas to Trump aides seeking to monitor election integrity. Flávio also cried watching video messages from his absent brothers Carlos and Eduardo and praised the mother of his daughters as his 'backbone'.

item.title: Caiado oficializa candidatura de olho em críticas a Flávio e Lula
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) officially launched his presidential bid at the party's national convention in São Paulo on July 26, with Gilberto Kassab as his vice-presidential running mate in a 'pure-blood' ticket. Despite the PSD holding positions in Lula's government, Kassab pledged an antagonistic stance to strengthen congressional backing and position Caiado as a third way amid Lula-Bolsonaro polarization. The campaign has already intensified criticism of both political poles, with Caiado claiming Lula may avoid debates out of fear of direct confrontation.

item.title: Tempo contra Flavio
item.description: DataFolha poll shows Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro by five percentage points in the runoff, outside the margin of error, giving encouragement to both candidates. Despite Lula's lead, Flávio remains competitive, and the poll did not capture a possible reconciliation between Michelle Bolsonaro and the PL candidate, suggesting potential to regain lost support among women and evangelicals.

item.title: Eleição no Brasil contaminou negociação com EUA, dizem ex-embaixadores
item.description: Former ambassadors say Brazil's electoral period has contaminated trade negotiations with the United States, as the government politicized the tariff dispute with partisan interests. Rubens Barbosa argues that mixing foreign policy with partisanship harms national interests and that the U.S., under Trump, has adopted a 'law of the jungle' approach, imposing tariffs on Brazil in retaliation for alleged persecution of Bolsonaro. He advises Brazil to wait until January 2026 to resume negotiations with a clear strategy, avoiding foreign interference and disinformation during the election period.

item.title: Fake news e novos modelos de pesquisas: os desafios do TSE para 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) is preparing for the 2026 elections with a focus on combating disinformation, malicious use of artificial intelligence, political and gender-based violence, and implementing a new model for registering electoral polls. TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques has partnered with major digital platforms to intensify efforts against false content, emphasizing that this election will be the most digitalized in Brazil's history.

item.title: Tarifaço de Trump expõe limites do Brasil para elevar participação no comércio global
item.description: The Lula government seeks to expand Brazilian markets following U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, but faces the challenge of low global trade integration despite the Brazil Sovereign program's subsidized credit. The credit strategy failed to significantly boost Brazil's participation in international production chains.
